author: Georgi Kalchev (https://402cron.com)
description: Paid cron for AI agents: we call your https URL on schedule, signed. No account, paid with x402.
name: 402cron

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.title: Pricing and payment requirements
tools.description: What a delivery costs, which packs exist, and the exact x402 payment requirements for each. Balance is counted in DELIVERIES, not money, and packs never expire. Call this before buying.

tools.name: get_docs
tools.title: Machine documentation
tools.description: One section of the machine documentation: quickstart, headers, signature, notice, errors, billing or limits. Omit `section` to get the whole document.

section.description: Which section to return. Omit for all of it.

tools.name: get_service_status
tools.title: Is the service selling right now
tools.description: Whether the service is currently selling, on which network, and if not — why not. This is configuration, not liveness: the full health endpoint is at /health.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.title: List your scheduled tasks
tools.description: Your tasks and their state. Needs your management token as an Authorization header on this connection.

state.description: Filter by state: live (default), all, or one exact state such as active or paused_by_client.

tools.title: One task with its full state
tools.description: A single task: schedule, destination, state, next run, and how many failures in a row it carries.

id.description: Task id (UUID), as returned by create_task or list_tasks.

tools.name: create_task
tools.title: Create or update a scheduled task
tools.description: Register a schedule against a destination you have already verified. Idempotent on "name": the same name updates the existing task instead of creating a second one. Creating costs nothing; each delivery ATTEMPT costs one credit.

name.description: Your name for the task. Unique among your live tasks; creating with an existing name updates it.

cron.description: 5 fields, UTC only, one minute at the finest. Operators: * a-b a,b */n a-b/n. Names: SUN-SAT (day), JAN-DEC (month). Macros: @yearly @annually @monthly @weekly @daily @midnight @hourly. Day-of-week is 0-6 with 0 = Sunday; 7 also means Sunday. Write days as names (MON-FRI). Numbers differ between schedulers: Quartz, AWS EventBridge and Cloudflare number Sunday as 1, we and croniter as 0. Translated for you: "?". "?" as a whole day-of-month or day-of-week field becomes "*". A NUMERIC day-of-week next to "?" is refused, because "?" means the expression was written where Sunday is 1. Refused: Quartz L, Quartz W, Quartz #, six fields (seconds), seven fields (year), @reboot, @every, CRON_TZ= prefixes, time zones of any kind — each with a code saying what to send instead.

url.description: The https:// destination. It must already be registered and verified — see register_destination.

method.description: HTTP method of the delivery. Default POST. GET and HEAD carry no body.

timeoutMs.description: How long we wait for your server, 250-2000 ms. Answer 202 and do the work behind it.

headers.description: Headers we send with the delivery. Stored ENCRYPTED at rest — put credentials here, never in the body.

body.description: The body we send. Stored in the clear, so it must not carry credentials. A non-string is serialized as JSON.

annotations.title: Create or update a scheduled task

tools.name: pause_task
tools.title: Pause a task
tools.description: Stop firing until you resume. Nothing is charged while a task is paused.

id.description: Task id (UUID), as returned by create_task or list_tasks.

tools.name: resume_task
tools.title: Resume a paused task
tools.description: Start firing again on the schedule. Refused if your balance is empty — buy deliveries first.

id.description: Task id (UUID), as returned by create_task or list_tasks.

tools.name: run_task_now
tools.title: Fire a task once, right now
tools.description: Deliver immediately, outside the schedule. THIS COSTS ONE CREDIT per attempt, exactly like a scheduled firing, and a timeout or unreachable host is retried up to three times — so one call can cost up to three credits. Use it to test a destination.

id.description: Task id (UUID), as returned by create_task or list_tasks.

annotations.title: Fire a task once, right now

tools.name: delete_task
tools.title: Delete a task
tools.description: Move the task to the recycle bin. It stops firing immediately and can be restored for 30 days with restore_task; after that it is unrecoverable. Credits already spent are not refunded.

id.description: Task id (UUID), as returned by create_task or list_tasks.

tools.name: restore_task
tools.title: Restore a deleted task
tools.description: Bring a task back from the recycle bin within 30 days. It comes back PAUSED — resume it explicitly.

id.description: Task id (UUID), as returned by create_task or list_tasks.

tools.name: register_destination
tools.title: Register a destination URL
tools.description: Claim an https:// URL you control. We answer with a challenge and a SIGNING SECRET that is shown ONCE and never again — store it before you do anything else; it is what lets you verify that a delivery really came from us. The permission covers that path and everything beneath it, nothing above. Verification is one request from us to the exact URL you registered: POST, headers X-402cron-Challenge: <value> and X-402cron-Event: verify, JSON body {"challenge":"<value>"}. Reply within 5 seconds, without a redirect, with a body that is the bare value or {"challenge":"<value>"}; we read the first 512 bytes and do not check the HTTP status (2xx is fine). Then call POST /api/destinations/{id}/verify within 15 minutes of registering. A fixed-response webhook cannot pass: you need an endpoint you can program. Registering a URL that is still pending issues a new challenge and a new signing secret every time — the old secret immediately stops verifying deliveries; a verified URL is left untouched unless you add ?rotate=1. The daily verification allowance (10 per destination, 40 per client, UTC day) does not reset on re-registration.

tools.name: verify_destination
tools.title: Verify a registered destination
tools.description: Verification is one request from us to the exact URL you registered: POST, headers X-402cron-Challenge: <value> and X-402cron-Event: verify, JSON body {"challenge":"<value>"}. Reply within 5 seconds, without a redirect, with a body that is the bare value or {"challenge":"<value>"}; we read the first 512 bytes and do not check the HTTP status (2xx is fine). Then call POST /api/destinations/{id}/verify within 15 minutes of registering. A fixed-response webhook cannot pass: you need an endpoint you can program. Registering a URL that is still pending issues a new challenge and a new signing secret every time — the old secret immediately stops verifying deliveries; a verified URL is left untouched unless you add ?rotate=1. The daily verification allowance (10 per destination, 40 per client, UTC day) does not reset on re-registration. Until this passes, no task may point at the destination.

id.description: Destination id, as returned by register_destination.

tools.name: list_destinations
tools.title: List your destinations
tools.description: The URLs you have claimed and whether each is verified. The signing secrets are never shown again.

tools.name: delete_destination
tools.title: Delete a destination
tools.description: Remove a claimed URL. Refused while a task still points at it — delete the task first.

id.description: Destination id, as returned by register_destination.
